recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-7568 unless the Security work group later decides to remodel Provenance.entity.agent or the single-activity Provenance guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-7568 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Security issue asking how Provenance agents and entities are linked when multiple agents and entities participate in the activity that resulted in the target resource; the Jira resolution says it was resolved by 9840.
initial_application: No direct FHIR-7568 commit was found. The linked resolution was applied through git commit 7755ff73d634727ea105334aa4aa76f05df7cbd1, which included GF#9840 and changed Provenance.entity.agent from 0..1 to 0..* while adding the explanatory comment about an agent providing access to an externally managed entity used in the Provenance activity.
additional_context: Provenance is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition preserves the FHIR-9840 cardinality and comment on Provenance.entity.agent, while the Provenance introduction says a Provenance resource corresponds to a single activity and multiple activities are represented by independent Provenance records. FHIR-7570, a companion clarification, is already represented on the combined branch. Later Published issue FHIR-33228 intentionally changed the same definition from generated to used, confirming the current source-entity wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already answers the FHIR-7568 question through the active Provenance.entity.agent definition/comment and cardinality, interpreted with the related FHIR-9840 and FHIR-33228 decisions.
